title: A non-pth-power in a finite type characteristic-p domain is detected by a derivation
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $B$ an integral domain with $p=0$ in $B$, with fraction field $M$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume that there are a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring $(R_0,\mathfrak m_0)$ which is $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and a ring map $R_0\to B$ of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $f\in B$ be an element which is not a $p$th power in $M$. Then there is a derivation $D:B\to B$ (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) with $D(f)\neq0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PH (lemma-find-D), line 11860 and proof

proof.text: (Replace $R_0$ by its image.) Let $\mathfrak p=\ker(R_0\to B)$ and $\bar R=R_0/\mathfrak p$, identified with the image of $R_0$ in $B$. As $B$ is a domain, $1\ne0$ in $B$, so $\mathfrak p\ne R_0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] $\bar R$ is a Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m_0/\mathfrak p$, which is $\bar{\mathfrak m}$-adically complete. Being a subring of $B$, $\bar R$ is a domain with $p=0$ in $\bar R$. Elements of $B$ generating $B$ as an $R_0$-algebra also generate it as an $\bar R$-algebra, so $\bar R\subseteq B$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PH (lemma-find-D, line 11860), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: (Replace $\bar R$ by a power series ring over a field.) By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] applied to the Noetherian complete local domain $\bar R$ there is a subring $R_1\subseteq\bar R$ over which $\bar R$ is a finitely generated module, with $R_1\cong k[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a field $k$ or $R_1\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$. The second case is impossible: in a Cohen ring the maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ is nonzero [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], so $p\ne0$ in $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], whereas $p=0$ in $R_1\subseteq B$. Hence $R_1=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ ($x_i$ the image of $X_i$), and $p=0$ in $k\subseteq R_1\subseteq B$, so $k$ has characteristic $p$; $R_1$ is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1), and $R_1\to B$ is injective (an inclusion of subrings). $B$ is of finite type over $R_1$: if $r_1,\ldots,r_s$ generate $\bar R$ as an $R_1$-module and $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ generate $B$ as an $\bar R$-algebra, then every element of $B$ is a polynomial in the $b_j$ with coefficients $\sum_lc_lr_l$, $c_l\in R_1$, so $r_1,\ldots,r_s,b_1,\ldots,b_t$ generate $B$ as an $R_1$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PH (lemma-find-D, line 11860), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: (Noether normalization and the element $f'$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-noether-normalization-over-domain] applied to the injective finite type map $R_1\to B$ of Step 2 ($R_1$ a domain) there are $d\ge0$, $y_1,\ldots,y_d\in B$, an $R_1$-subalgebra $B'\subseteq B$ and a nonzero $g\in R_1$ such that $A:=R_1[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\subseteq B'$ is a polynomial ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_d]$ over $R_1$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $B'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, and $B'_g\to B_g$ is bijective. $B'$ is a domain with $p=0$, and $g\ne0$ in $B$. Surjectivity of $B'_g\to B_g$ gives, for every $b\in B$, some $b'\in B'$ and $e\ge0$ with $b/1=b'/g^e$ in $B_g$, i.e. $g^u(g^eb-b')=0$ for some $u$, hence $g^eb=b'\in B'$ since $B$ is a domain. Consequently every element of $B$, hence of $M$, is a quotient of elements of $B'$: the fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of $B'$ is $M$. Applying this to $b=f$, choose $e$ with $g^ef\in B'$ and $N\ge0$ with $pN\ge e$; then $f':=g^{pN}f=g^{pN-e}(g^ef)\in B'$. And $f'$ is not a $p$th power in $M$: $f'=h^p$ with $h\in M$ would give $f=(h/g^N)^p$.

The family $(E_J)_J$ of subfields of $M$ satisfies (i)-(iii) for the field $M$: $M^p\subseteq E_J$; $ igcap_JE_J=M^p$; and $E_{J\cup J'}\subseteq E_J\cap E_{J'}$ because $K_{J\cup J'}\subseteq K_J\cap K_{J'}$ (part (4)). split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 07PH (more-algebra.tex, lemma-find-D) and its proof; statement kept (it agrees with 07PH, the complete local ring named (R_0, m_0)). Proof written in 6 steps following the source: image of R_0 is a complete local domain (0325 node); 032D node gives R_1 finite under it, the Cohen-ring case excluded since p = 0; Noether normalization over a domain (07NA, new node) gives A = R_1[y] in B' in B with B'_g = B_g, f' = g^{pN} f in B', fraction field of B' is M; reduction to B' by the last sentence of 07PE (new node; the existing lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends states only items (1), (2)) with the computation D(f') = g^{pN} D(f) written out; for B' finite over A: M/K finite (integrality), df' != 0 by 031W (new), p-basis (07P2, new), the subfields K_J (07P5, new) and 07P4 (1), (2) (new; the source leaves its use implicit) give J with df' != 0 in Omega_{M/M^pK_J}; a linear form (Mathlib leaf Module.Projective.exists_dual_ne_zero) and the universal property give a K_J-derivation, multiplied by the product of denominators of its values on A_J-module generators. 7 new nodes (6 unsplit, 1 Mathlib leaf). Duplicate found: lem-weil-pbc-find-derivation-not-pth-power states the same lemma (07PH), created the same day for lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular; reported for a merge. lean.statement: theorem exists_apply_ne_zero_of_not_pth_power (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CharP B p] (M : Type v) [Field M] [Algebra B M] [IsFractionRing B M] (R₀ : Type w) [CommRing R₀] [IsNoetherianRing R₀] [IsLocalRing R₀] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀) R₀] [Algebra R₀ B] [Algebra.FiniteType R₀ B] (f : B) (hf : ¬ ∃ x : M, x ^ p = algebraMap B M f) : ∃ D : Derivation ℤ B B, D f ≠ 0

reviewed_lean.note: p prime=Fact p.Prime; B domain p=0=IsDomain+CharP B p; M=IsFractionRing B M; R0 Noetherian local m0-adically complete=IsNoetherianRing+IsLocalRing+IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R0) R0; R0->B finite type=Algebra.FiniteType; f not pth power in M=not exists x:M, x^p=algebraMap f; additive Leibniz D:B->B with D f /= 0 = exists D : Derivation Z B B
